title: 2023 Discovery Coverage A/B Audit: Sparse Hub v3.2 vs Legacy Quarterly Discovery
contaminationNote: This audit was created only after the v3.2 run was locked and freshly revealed. Legacy 2023 outcomes were not read before the v3.2 selection digest was frozen.

headline.conclusion: The dominant recall bottleneck is now hub-ingestion coverage, not lack of causal-neighborhood reasoning. Eighteen hand-picked hub items per year are not a defensible proxy for a Bloomberg/Wind/LSEG weekly information stream.

missTaxonomy.hub_intake_miss: A material event was present in broad professional/generalist coverage but was not included in the frozen hub denominator.
missTaxonomy.association_miss: The broad hub event was ingested but the economically relevant second/third-order expression was not generated or verified.
missTaxonomy.mapping_underwriting_miss: The event and relevant economic mechanism were covered, but the company expression, expectation burden, timing or selection decision was inferior.
missTaxonomy.no_actionable_miss: The event was absent or rejected, but later evidence shows no meaningful lost opportunity under the frozen 60d benchmark test.

cases.interpretation: Both systems understood the coal-price-to-power-margin mechanism and both failed. v3.2 chose a less-bad expression but this is not a discovery-recall problem.

v3.2 recognized the throughput-vs-spend divergence but rejected airport exposure due high expectation burden. Legacy airline selection was only a small 60d excess loser. This is not evidence for loosening the v3.2 gate.

broadHubEvidenceAvailable.claim: Battery-grade lithium carbonate had risen for ten consecutive sessions and rebounded about 35.6% from the late-April low.
Lithium carbonate approached RMB300k/t after a rapid rebound from below RMB180k/t.

cases.interpretation: The sparse hub feed failed to ingest a clearly visible broad-market event. The missed legacy selection later failed, so this miss did not cost return, but it proves the source universe was incomplete.

This is the cleanest evidence for causal-neighborhood value. The same broad state change produced a failed obvious first-order automaker expression in legacy discovery but a successful second-order scarce ro-ro-capacity expression in v3.2.
A positive legacy opportunity was absent from the 18-item hub denominator. The loss is attributable to sparse intake before association is even attempted.

broadHubEvidenceAvailable.claim: The global memory rout, inventory glut and producer capex/output cuts were repeatedly covered as a major cycle event.
Samsung's profit decline slowed, with AI-related demand identified as important to memory-price recovery.

cases.interpretation: The sparse hub feed missed a broad global semiconductor cycle that generalist Bloomberg coverage repeatedly surfaced.

broadHubEvidenceAvailable.claim: Samsung said the memory recovery was taking hold after profit beat expectations.

cases.interpretation: Again the intake was incomplete, though the missed legacy trade later failed. Dense ingestion must improve recall without implying automatic promotion.

broadHubEvidenceAvailable.claim: A-share supplier disclosure showed 400G optical modules in mass production and 800G silicon-photonics modules ready for small-batch delivery.
Another supplier reported 800G optical-module products entering small-batch supply.

cases.interpretation: This is the most expensive miss. The broad AI/high-speed interconnect transition was visible in professional/generalist coverage, but the 18-item v3.2 denominator never ingested the event family, so causal association had no chance to operate.

conclusions: v3.2 improves expression search when the broad event is actually ingested.
Sparse hand-picked hub samples create a false ceiling on opportunity frequency and can miss the year's highest-value opportunity family.
The next change must target source-ingestion completeness while leaving v3.2 causal association and downstream underwriting unchanged.
More hub items must not imply more selections: dense ingest, sparse promotion.
prohibitedInference: Do not conclude that all legacy misses should have been selected. Several missed families later lost money. The audit diagnoses event-universe incompleteness, not a reason to relax underwriting.
